q: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different _____.
e: Isotopes of an element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, resulting in different masses.

q: Isotopes have the same number of _____ but a different number of _____.
e: By definition, isotopes share the same proton count (atomic number) but vary in neutron count.

q: Isotopes have the same _____ number but different _____ number.
e: Isotopes are characterized by having the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

q: Because isotopes have the same number of electrons, they have the same _____ properties.
e: Chemical properties are determined by electron configuration, which is identical for all isotopes of a given element.

q: Isotopes have different _____ properties as they vary in their atomic mass.
e: Physical properties, such as density and diffusion rate, depend on atomic mass and thus differ among isotopes.

q: Stable isotopes do not decay, whereas unstable isotopes are _____ and decay into other elements.
e: Unstable isotopes are radioactive (radioisotopes) and undergo radioactive decay to achieve a more stable configuration.

q: Isotopes can be produced artificially using nuclear reactors and _____.
e: Artificial isotopes are commonly synthesized in nuclear reactors or particle accelerators.

q: The stable isotope $^{63}_{29}\text{Cu}$ has 29 protons, 29 electrons, and _____ neutrons.
e: The number of neutrons is the mass number minus the atomic number: $63 - 29 = 34$.

q: The natural abundance of $^{63}_{29}\text{Cu}$ is _____, while $^{65}_{29}\text{Cu}$ is 31%.
e: In nature, the stable isotope $^{63}_{29}\text{Cu}$ has a natural abundance of 69%.

q: The three isotopes of hydrogen are hydrogen ($^1_1\text{H}$), deuterium ($^2_1\text{H}$), and _____.
e: The three isotopes of hydrogen are protium (hydrogen), deuterium, and tritium.

q: Among the hydrogen isotopes, _____ is radioactive and transforms into the helium isotope $^3_2\text{He}$.
e: Tritium is the only radioactive isotope of hydrogen, decaying into helium-3.

q: The most abundant isotope in the entire universe is the hydrogen isotope _____.
e: Ordinary hydrogen ($^1_1\text{H}$) is the most abundant isotope in the universe.
